answer: A graduated trust limit works like a narrow inlet: every new agent starts able to move only tiny amounts, no matter how many identities it spawns. Its allowance widens only after a history of completed, dispute-free trades, so a sybil farm must patiently earn trust for each puppet, paying time and fees per identity. Like a sonnet that only earns its final couplet by following the form, and a juniper that grows slowly but holds its ground, reputation here is earned gradually, making mass fake identities expensive and slow rather than free.
